title: AVMD-ST: attention-variational mode decomposition based spectrogram transformer for differential diagnosis of asthma and COPD
task: Differential diagnosis of asthma vs COPD using lung sound analysis
key_results: 95.75% classification accuracy on pooled dataset (AIIMS Raipur + ICBHI 2017 + KAUH); successfully distinguished asthma and COPD from healthy controls using acoustic biomarkers
comments: Subject-wise train/test split appropriately prevents data leakage, but external validation on truly independent cohorts would strengthen clinical applicability claims.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FIR-filtered VMD-derived intrinsic mode functions can isolate clinically significant respiratory features (wheezes, crackles) for improved classification
hypotheses.result: Achieved 95.75% accuracy, demonstrating effective feature isolation and Transformer-based temporal dependency capture

title: Evaluation of acute FGF2 and PRDX3 for long COVID prediction across cohorts and proteomic platforms
task: Predicting Long COVID risk using acute phase blood proteins across cohorts and platforms
key_results: FGF2 and PRDX3 proteins did not reliably improve prediction beyond age and sex; optimism-corrected Brier score difference was +0.00342 (95% CI: -0.00608 to +0.02834) in Su cohort and +0.01093 (-0.01721 to +0.03882) in transferred Zurich model
comments: The finding of negligible predictive gain combined with platform-dependent protein standardization highlights critical challenges in cross-cohort proteomic model translation for clinical risk prediction.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Acute-phase FGF2 and PRDX3 levels improve Long COVID prediction beyond demographic factors
hypotheses.result: No reliable improvement; inconclusive and inconsistent performance across Su and Zurich cohorts with overlapping confidence intervals

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fixed protein-assay mappings and within-cohort standardization enable cross-platform model transfer
hypotheses.result: Failed; transferred models overpredicted risk in Zurich and standardization pipeline was deemed not ready for individualized patient prediction

title: Nature-inspired antenna design using hybrid ANN and Bayesian optimization techniques for biomedical applications
task: Antenna design optimization for WBAN biomedical applications using surrogate modelling and multi-objective optimization
key_results: Compact antenna (0.2968λ₀mm × 0.318λ₀mm) at 3.18 GHz with impedance bandwidth 3.10–3.285 GHz; excellent agreement between simulated and fabricated results
comments: Hybrid ANN+Bayesian approach is systematic; comparison of NSGA-II, MOPSO, GWO, and BO+GPR provides useful guidance, though specific performance metrics across optimizers are not quantified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bayesian optimization with Gaussian process regression outperforms evolutionary algorithms for antenna DGS tuning
hypotheses.result: Achieved optimized compact design suitable for WBAN; surrogate modelling reduced computational cost vs. full EM simulation

title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
task: Enhancing superconducting qubit fidelity via nonreciprocal diodes in twisted materials
key_results: 1° twist in NbSe2 achieves 27.6% diode efficiency enhancement over pristine devices
Intermediate efficiency (27.6%) demonstrated as optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and two-level system stability
comments: Counter-intuitive finding that sub-optimal rectification outperforms maximal efficiency for quantum information processing; practical design guidance for twisted superconductor applications.

model_io.model: Twisted NbSe2 quantum diode under magnetic fields

hypotheses.hypothesis: Maximal rectification efficiency improves qubit fidelity
hypotheses.result: Rejected; intermediate efficiency proves superior for preserving anharmonicity and two-level dynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: 1° twist enhances diode efficiency in NbSe2
